gaps.sentence: Have you met the couple ___ son is in your class?
gaps.hint: the son belongs to the couple
gaps.explanation: 'Whose son' means 'their son'; the possessive relative 'whose' is required.

gaps.sentence: Mrs Patterson, ___ taught me maths, has just retired.
gaps.hint: extra information after a comma about a person
gaps.explanation: After a comma the relative clause is non-defining, so 'that' is impossible and 'who' refers to the person.

gaps.sentence: ___ mattered most was that nobody had been hurt.
gaps.explanation: 'What' = the thing that; it acts as subject of the clause.

gaps.sentence: The reason ___ the flight was diverted has never been made public.
gaps.explanation: 'The reason why' — 'why' is the relative for reasons.

gaps.sentence: The programme ___ I watched last night was about volcanoes.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to things, even when it is the object of the clause.

gaps.sentence: She has three daughters, all of ___ are at university.
gaps.explanation: 'All of whom' refers to people after 'of'; 'all of which' is for things and 'all of them' cannot join the clauses after a comma.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ produces these parts has factories in three countries.
gaps.explanation: A company takes 'which' as subject; 'who' is normally reserved for individual people.

gaps.sentence: The house at the end of the street, ___ has been empty for years, is for sale.
gaps.explanation: Non-defining clauses about things take 'which'; 'who' is for people and 'that' is not allowed here.
